prompt: An industrial water pump has an efficiency of 65% and delivers 13 kW of useful mechanical power to water flowing through a pipeline. At what rate is energy dissipated as heat in the pump mechanism?

answer.explanation: Total input power P_in = P_useful / eta = 13 kW / 0.65 = 20 kW. Wasted power = P_in - P_useful = 20 kW - 13 kW = 7.0 kW.

distractor_explanations: Correct. P_in = 13 / 0.65 = 20 kW. Dissipated power = 20 - 13 = 7.0 kW.
Incorrect. 4.55 kW is 35% of the useful power: 0.35 * 13 = 4.55 kW (taking 35% of output instead of input).
Incorrect. 8.45 kW is 65% of the useful power: 0.65 * 13 = 8.45 kW.
Incorrect. 13 kW is the useful power itself.
hints: First find the total electrical power input using P_in = P_useful / eta.
Then subtract the useful power from the total input power.
solution: Efficiency eta = P_useful / P_in => P_in = P_useful / eta = 13 kW / 0.65 = 20 kW. By conservation of power: P_in = P_useful + P_wasted => P_wasted = P_in - P_useful = 20 kW - 13 kW = 7.0 kW. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Warn against the common error of multiplying useful power by 0.35: wasted power is 35% of INPUT power, not output power.
Walk through P_in calculation first to establish the correct base value.
